nodes.label: Allocation Params View
nodes.rationale: Documents the sizer pipeline in one sentence: 'Kelly weight x caps x regime multiplier x leverage, then converted to contracts via FX and contract-size tables.'

nodes.label: Fractional Kelly and Weight Caps
nodes.rationale: fractional_kelly scales full Kelly (0.25 = quarter Kelly); per_symbol_cap is a hard ceiling on any single symbol's weight; aggregate_cap is a hard ceiling on the sum of weights. Caps are applied after the Kelly fraction so a mis-estimated mu/sigma cannot blow past a known bound.

nodes.label: Regime Multiplier Table
nodes.rationale: The sizer multiplies the Kelly weight by a per-regime factor keyed on the Brain's current label. This is the second, continuous use of the regime signal (size scaling) as opposed to the Strategy Master's discrete use (eligible / not eligible).

nodes.label: FX and Contract Size Conversion
nodes.rationale: fx_inr_per_usd converts bucket capital in INR to the broker quote currency (USD on Delta India); a per-symbol contract_sizes table converts notional into contract counts, with default_contract_size as the fallback for symbols missing from the table.

nodes.label: Per-Symbol Kelly Stats (mu / sigma)
nodes.rationale: Per-symbol mu_per_period / sigma_per_period must be sourced from the (separate) backtester; the sizer plugs them into f* = mu / sigma^2. When a symbol has no stats the sizer falls back to default_for_unknown rather than refusing to size, and the view says so explicitly so an empty stats table is not read as 'no trading'.
